title: test-0076-SOC-CIV-LIVELIHOODS
passage: Teacher: Today we are discussing livelihoods. Ravi, do all farmers own the land they work on? Ravi: I think so, they must have their own plots. Teacher: Actually, many landless labourers work on others' fields for daily wages. They often struggle because they only find work during sowing and harvesting seasons. What about city jobs, Meena? Meena: I believe everyone in a city has a permanent job with benefits like pensions and medical leave. Teacher: That is a common misunderstanding. While some have formal jobs, many people are street vendors or daily wage earners who have no such security. They work extremely hard from early morning to late at night to earn a living. It is not about laziness, but about the lack of formal opportunities. Many vendors face constant pressure to clear their spots and have no fixed income. So, livelihoods vary greatly based on whether one is a landless labourer, a small farmer, or a street vendor. Understanding these differences helps us see why some families struggle more than others to meet their basic needs throughout the year.
summary: Ravi, do all farmers own the land they work on? Teacher: Many landless workers work on others' fields for daily wages. They often struggle because they only work during the sowing and harvesting seasons.
